messages:
jess_acme: Hey team — after our infra team applied a new ModSecurity ruleset at ~03:10 UTC we started seeing 401 invalid_api_key on calls from our backend. Nothing changed in code. Using a Lambda -> internal API gateway -> nginx -> redwood. Sample curl works from my machine. Any ideas?

maria_support: Hi Jess — can you paste the raw request headers from the failing requests (redact key) and the exact Authorization header line if possible?

jess_acme: here are headers captured by our gateway (redacted):

-----
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Api-Key "sk_3q...Yz=="
User-Agent: my-service/1.2.3
X-Forwarded-For: 1.2.3.4
-----

maria_support: aha — I see quotes around the key. Try removing the surrounding quotes; headers shouldn't have literal \" characters. Can you show your gateway/nginx config? Some WAF rules also strip or rewrite headers.

devon_oncall: pinging infra — also check for mod_security rule that blocks headers containing 'Api-Key' or 'Authorization' patterns. We had a case where ModSec 2141592 removed headers with 'Api-Key' substring.

tyler_csm: customer says curl from their local machine works, fails from their prod origin.

jess_acme: nginx snippet from our gateway:

location /proxy {
  proxy_pass https://api.redwood.com;
  proxy_set_header Authorization "$http_authorization";
  # modsec applied at http layer
}

Also we run a gateway Lua script that sanitizes headers:

if header:match('Api%-Key') then header = header:gsub('\"','') end

We thought it was removing quotes but maybe something else.

maria_support: Two quick suspects:
1) ModSecurity/WAF rule stripping the header entirely (Redwood sees no auth) -> 401 invalid_api_key.
2) Gateway is adding extra quotes or encoding. From your headers earlier the Authorization line includes quotes — that will make the key literal include quotes and fail.

Can you grep your ingress logs for the outgoing request to Redwood to confirm whether Authorization header is present and exact value? Example command we use:

sudo tcpdump -s 0 -A 'host api.redwood.com and port 443'  # or check gateway debug logs

jess_acme: infra ran a quick check; the gateway log shows requests to redwood with the header removed entirely (Authorization not present). They found ModSec rule id 981246 set to drop headers matching /Api-Key/i

devon_oncall: OK — that's the root cause. ModSecurity rule dropping the header before proxy. Two options:
- Allowlist the Authorization header in the WAF (recommended)
- Rewrite/redact on ingress but restore before proxying (add custom header like X-Internal-Auth and set proxy_set_header Authorization $http_x_internal_auth)

maria_support: For short term ask infra to turn that rule to DetectionOnly for your service and confirm requests succeed. If you prefer a longer term fix we can support a recommended header rewrite. Let me know once infra toggles the rule and we can re-test.

jess_acme: infra flipped the rule to detection-only and requests are green again. Thanks all! :tada:

maria_support: Great — I'll follow up with a short KB entry for customers who hit WAFs. Closing after infra decides whether to allowlist or use header rewrite. :white_check_mark:
